Done. `out/T1/model.safetensors` has 184 tensors and matches the spec bit-exactly (verified independently against the input: key set, shapes, dtypes and values all match the required renumbering).

**Plan** (`out/T1/plan.yaml`): `delete` blocks 2/6/10/14 by escaped-dot pattern, then 10 `move`s in ascending old-index order (3→2 … 15→11) using a capture-group rewrite, then the three required asserts.

**Two executions**, one failure: `assert: { count: { of: ..., is: 0 } }` cannot express absence — `count.of` resolves its reference first and raises `matched zero tensors` before comparing. Swapped to `assert: { not: { exists: 'gpt_neox\.layers\.1[2-5]\..*' } }`, whose payload is a bare tensor-ref rather than a `{ of: ... }` mapping.

The renumbering-collision hazard was handled by ordering moves ascending; `move` refuses existing destinations, so a wrong order would have failed loudly instead of silently overwriting. Self-report is in `out/T1/REPORT.md`.
